regressionFixedThisSession: LiveRecordingTest.fencedHungShardKeepsSessionLeaseUntilWriterTerminates() failed nondeterministically on Windows: PacketEngine.close()/CaptureWriter.close() intentionally do not join the writer thread (a hung writer must not block shutdown), so the test could return, and JUnit's @TempDir cleanup could run, while the writer daemon thread was still mid-write. Windows cannot delete a directory containing an open file handle (POSIX can), producing DirectoryNotEmptyException. Fixed by having the test await ReplayQuota IO/PROMOTION usage reaching zero (proof the writer actually finished) before returning, matching the pattern already used in the sibling recording test. No production code changed.

semanticModelingWorkThisSession: Closed all 24 remaining mandatory gaps (block_entity_data, chunk_batch_start/finished, chunks_biomes, container_set_content/data/slot, damage_event, entity_event, explode(enhanced), level_chunk_with_light, light_update, move_minecart_along_track, player_look_at, respawn, section_blocks_update, set_cursor_item/entity_data/equipment/player_inventory, and serverbound container_button_click/container_click/container_slot_state_changed, plus bundle_delimiter which was previously METADATA-ONLY). Built a modern data-component item model (SemanticPayload.Item: empty flag, registry-key type, count, explicitly typed damage/maxDamage/unbreakable/enchantments fields, and a bounded/sorted/deduplicated otherComponents registry-key disclosure list for every other component, so ordering never depends on native map iteration order) rather than wrapping legacy NBT/ItemMeta. ServerboundContainerClickPacket's changed-slot/carried-item semantics are represented as index+empty/non-empty only (ContainerClickClaim/ChangedSlot), because the native HashedStack type genuinely exposes no content accessor (verified by inspecting its pinned bytecode: only a matches(ItemStack,HashGenerator) equality check exists) - the model deliberately does not fabricate item identity that was never on the wire. Chunk/light data stays compact: ChunkBaseline and LightUpdate carry chunk identity, bounded encoded byte lengths, and block-entity/heightmap/section counts, never per-block or per-light-value objects. Registry identity is modeled as a normalized String key (via BuiltInRegistries/Holder.unwrapKey(), which fails closed with IllegalArgumentException on an unregistered holder) - no ResourceKey/Holder/NMS type crosses the platform boundary. Unknown-but-relevant data (extra components, opaque entity-data serializer values) is disclosed as bounded identity/kind-only facts, never silently dropped and never leaked as raw native objects. All new records are bounded against pathological input (component/enchantment/changed-slot/entity-data-field counts capped, text tagged and length-checked) and have symmetric SemanticCodec round-trip support exercised by ReplayTest's fixture list. Native verification used real pinned bytecode throughout, including two techniques not previously needed in this codebase: VanillaRegistries.createLookup() + Holder.Reference.bindComponents(DataComponentMap.EMPTY) to legally construct real registered ItemStack/enchantment/damage-type holders in a test-only bootstrap (extensive javap-based research found no reachable caller of bindComponents from a minimal Bootstrap.bootStrap() harness; this calls the real public API directly rather than reproducing an untraced full dedicated-server startup sequence), and sun.misc.Unsafe.allocateInstance() field-injection for ClientboundLevelChunkPacketData/ClientboundLightUpdatePacketData/ClientboundLevelChunkWithLightPacket, whose only public constructors require a real LevelChunk/LevelLightEngine - the allocated objects are still the real native classes the normalizer reflects into, just constructed without running world-dependent business logic. Found and fixed two real bugs via this process: an inverted boolean in SemanticCodec's Item read helper (write side encodes true=empty, read side originally treated true=non-empty, causing every item-carrying payload to desynchronize on round-trip), and a nonexistent getBuffer() accessor assumed on ClientboundLevelChunkPacketData (the real class only exposes a private write buffer and a getReadBuffer() FriendlyByteBuf; the raw buffer field must be read directly, matching the pattern already used for blockEntitiesData). Also fixed an architecture-test violation introduced by an explanatory Javadoc comment that spelled out a net.minecraft.* fully-qualified name outside anticheat-platform-paper (the automated platform-isolation gate correctly does not distinguish comments from code) and updated one now-stale SemanticCoverageTest assertion that had hard-coded level_chunk_with_light as a permanently-missing example gap. Mandatory semantic gaps: 24 -> 0. Tests: 139 -> 162 (4 new native test classes: NativeInventoryTest 9, NativeEntityMiscTest 6, NativeWorldMiscTest 6, NativeChunkTest 2). No new inter-module dependency was added and no approved Phase 0 Markdown was modified. p1H2ReplayCheckpointWorkThisSession: Finished mid-session replay/checkpoint coverage. Schema: TransportCapsule gained a Checkpoint frame (startSequence/startGeneration/recordingEpoch/protocolState/captureEnabled/effectsMode/lastIngressOrdinal/certifiedIngressOrdinal/lastProcessingOrdinal/lastServerRevision) that must open a capsule if present, and an incompleteReason string field (empty when complete) so PREFIX INCOMPLETE always explains why (SEQUENCE_GAP/FRAME_COUNT_LIMIT/ROLLING_BUDGET_EXCEEDED/ROLLING_BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE_AT_START/EXPORT_ENCODE_FAILURE/DEGRADED), never just a bare boolean. TruthActor gained a package-private seed(...) method and HealthLatch a HealthLatch(long initialGeneration) constructor so TransportReplayDriver can resume validation exactly from a checkpoint's declared baseline instead of assuming every capsule starts at sequence 1 - proven by a negative-control test where a deliberately wrong checkpoint baseline produces a different (degraded) replay outcome. SessionRecording (already existing, now materially extended) supports pause()/resume() any number of times: pause() finalizes the current prefix as genuinely COMPLETE (a deliberate stop is not data loss) and exports it if a writer exists; resume() opens a fresh capsule seeded with a Checkpoint built from the session's real TruthActor.Snapshot/HealthLatch.State at that exact instant, never fabricating history before it. PacketEngine.enableRecording() no longer requires zero active sessions (relaxed precondition) and now broadcasts a RECORDING=true control to every already-active session, so capture can begin during an existing PLAY session, not only at connect time. Adaptive retention: LiveCapture's fair per-session rolling-budget share is now computed from the actual current active-session count (PacketEngine.activeSessionCount, a volatile field updated on every connect/remove) rather than the engine's static worst-case capacity, so light load gets more retained history while heavy load still respects the fixed 48MiB global cap (both directions verified by test); the existing per-owner ReplayQuota.reserve() accounting (unchanged) already prevented one noisy session from starving another's own fair share. Writer watchdog: CaptureWriter gained a Health enum (RUNNING/SLOW/HUNG/FENCED/TERMINATED) computed from an in-flight-job start timestamp against two fixed thresholds (2s/10s), plus fence() (stop admitting new jobs, touch nothing in-flight) - PacketEngine.supervise() now reports (once, not per-tick) when the writer is HUNG without ever releasing its leases, preserving the existing safety invariant that a resource charge is only released once termination is actually proven. Two real bugs were found and fixed via test failures during this work: SessionRecording.resume() computed a brand-new recording's Checkpoint elapsedNanos as (now - origin) where origin is captured a few nanoseconds AFTER the shard loop's own 'now' snapshot for a just-idle()'d recording, producing a spurious negative value that tripped Checkpoint's own clock-regression validation (fixed with Math.max(0, ...), documented as measurement-order noise, not a real regression); and SessionRecording.capture was a plain (non-volatile) field mutated by the shard thread but read via armed()/complete()/recordingEpoch() from other threads for diagnostics, with no visibility guarantee once the field's OWN value changed post-construction (the outer SessionRecording object reference stays the same across pause/resume, so Session.recording being volatile didn't help) - fixed by making SessionRecording.capture and recordingEpoch volatile.
p1H3RuntimeControlsWorkThisSession: Finished ordered runtime-control application. Two new Observation.Event/TransportCapsule.Event sealed variants (ControlChange(kind,value), CheckpointMarker(requestId)) flow through the exact same per-session ordering primitive packets already use: ConnectionIngress.bridge() (already existed, previously used only for server-authoritative Observation events) assigns them a real monotonic sequence number on the owning event-loop thread, so a control command submitted from a Bukkit command/operator thread is deterministically ordered relative to concurrently-arriving packets - not thread-timing luck. TruthActor requires zero changes: these events fall through process()'s existing preamble exactly like the pre-existing Tick event (advance processed/history/metrics, no packet-truth branch), so the packet-truth actor never gained any administrative-control awareness. PacketEngine.Shard.run() classifies each dequeued observation as administrative or not immediately after actor.process() runs for it (guaranteeing the checkpoint/control side effect reflects one coherent ordered instant, per the session-ownership requirement) and dispatches RECORDING toggles to SessionRecording.resume()/pause() and CheckpointMarker to an immediate export - proven end-to-end by a literal 'Packet A / Capture OFF / Packet B / Capture ON / Packet C / Checkpoint request / Packet D' test asserting the resulting sequence stays gap-free and healthy, plus a concurrent-submission variant. setCaptureEnabled() (the pre-existing engine-wide admission gate, deliberately left semantically unchanged - it is a blunt kill-switch, not a per-packet-stream toggle) is kept conceptually distinct from the new per-session RECORDING control to avoid conflating two different kinds of 'capture'; this distinction is documented so a reviewer does not read them as duplicates. suspendEffects()/new resumeEffects() now broadcast an EFFECTS_MODE marker into every active session's own ordered stream (a control epoch: replay/diagnostics can determine exactly which control state applied to which observation) and RuntimeControl gained a narrow resumeObservation() method that can only return to the safe OBSERVE_ONLY default from a stricter suspension - it structurally cannot reach ENFORCE, which remains reachable only through the untouched, still-unused RuntimeControl.enable(authorized, allGuardsQualified). Budget/guard records: new GuardStatus (capture/certification capability, effectsSuspended, overloaded, replayArmed, replayDurable, plus a productionQualified() that is a hardcoded false method, not a stored field, so it can never be anything else by construction), BudgetStatus (configured/effective capacity, active sessions, global/rolling/promotion/IO byte usage and limits, writer queue capacity/counters), and MonitoringSnapshot (bounded, aggregate-only engine-wide diagnostic - capture/effects mode, session/queue/journal aggregates, writer health, checkpoint/pause counters; no per-player field of any kind) exposed via new PacketEngine.guardStatus(UUID)/budgetStatus()/monitoringSnapshot() methods and surfaced in the /papea2ac status command output. Configuration validation (EngineConfiguration's existing strict parse/floor checks) was already in place and required no changes.
p1M1LocalWorkThisSession: Finished local callback-timing, monitoring, and fairness/backpressure qualification. PacketMetrics gained a Timer enum (CAPTURE_TO_PROCESS - the pre-existing capture-to-actor-process handoff latency, now named; CHECKPOINT_REQUEST_TO_EXPORT - new, isolates ordering/queueing delay specifically for operator checkpoint requests) with per-timer histograms, backward-compatible with every existing no-arg latency()/delayPercentileUpperBound() call site. CaptureWriter gained a small self-contained submit-to-start queue-delay histogram (queueDelayPercentileUpperBound/queueDelaySamples) rather than depending on anticheat-core's PacketMetrics, which would have been the wrong dependency direction (anticheat-replay does not and must not depend on anticheat-core) - this covers 'replay writer delay' from section 18 without a cross-module dependency change. No UUID/player-name label was added to any metric; every new measurement is a fixed, aggregate channel. Fairness/backpressure: new tests cover one flooded session's own control commands still being accepted and applied (they travel the small bridge mailbox, not the bounded packet ingress queue), many quiet sibling sessions making independent bounded progress under one noisy neighbor, queue saturation degrading health without ever falsely reporting certification available, and (from the P1-H2 section above) adaptive retention/no-starvation. Long-run/resource-accounting: a new LongRunRetentionTest runs 300 connect/toggle-recording-off/on/checkpoint/disconnect cycles and asserts PacketEngine.reservedBytes() returns to the exact same baseline after every single cycle (not just at the end), catching any per-cycle leak immediately rather than only in aggregate; a companion test runs 200 repeated writer-failure cycles and asserts zero IO/PROMOTION lease accumulation. Failure injection: disconnect racing an in-flight checkpoint request, one session's writer failure never touching a sibling's health, and shutdown during an in-flight export are all covered, each asserting zero engine-reported failures and full resource reclamation. All local M1 obligations are LOCAL-only, consistent with the task's own framing: real client and second-host qualification remain external.
hardeningPassThisSession: Focused hardening pass against three concrete risks an independent Senior Reviewer identified before running out of usage: (1) pre-login transport had per-connection bounds but no global admission bound; (2) the periodic pipeline audit might still check the pre-early-hook handler arrangement; (3) the PreLoginTransport->identity->Session binding lifecycle, buffer flush order, and shutdown ordering needed edge-case tracing. Full detail in docs/PHASE_1_HARDENING.md. Global pre-login admission: PaperCapture now tracks a global connection count (default cap 4096, non-static-final so tests can override) and aggregate journal-byte total (default cap 64MiB) across all not-yet-bound connections; a connection beyond the cap gets zero early-hook handlers installed and still becomes fully functional via the pre-existing attachFresh fallback, only missing pre-login-phase observations (new PRELOGIN_ADMISSION_REJECTED metric); the aggregate byte cap degrades individual journals the same way local overflow already did (new PRELOGIN_TRUNCATED_GLOBAL metric); both counters release on close or bind, guarded against double-release; bind() now also surfaces any truncation into session health (OVERLOADED), closing an adjacent pre-existing gap where truncation was never visible in coverage. Pipeline audit: found and fixed a real, previously undetected bug - audit()'s topology check compared pipeline.get("encoder")/pipeline.get("packet_handler") against Audit.encoder/Audit.dispatch fields that are populated ONLY by the attachFresh fallback path, never by bind() (the common early-hook path), meaning the periodic audit (every 20 ticks) would have unconditionally invalidated every early-hook-bound session's health as PIPELINE_UNCOVERED the first time it ran; never caught because no test exercised the periodic audit against a real, early-hook-bound session over time and the local smoke test never had a real player connected for it to audit. Fixed by re-deriving and recording which real topology attached each session (earlyHook/inboundAnchor/outboundAnchor) and auditing each against its own correct invariants. Binding races/buffer-flush/duplicate-login: traced and proven safe by test against the real PaperCapture with zero code changes needed, following from PreLoginTransport being channel-keyed, SessionKey being epoch-scoped, and Netty's single-threaded-per-channel event loop guarantee. Shutdown: one real gap found (a connection accepted right as unregisterEarlyHook() runs could still install permanent state referencing a discarded plugin instance), fixed with a closing flag checked before the reflective listener-removal completes. Stale control/replay events: proven safe by test, no code change needed. Resource accounting: audited every release path this pass touches; found and fixed one real bug (CaptureWriter incremented its failure counter before invoking the failure callback, a narrow real test race). Broad catch review: zero catch(Throwable)/catch(Exception) anywhere in production code, verified not changed. Package case: the on-disk anticheat-platform-paper source directory was still lowercase papea2ac while every package declaration inside was uppercase papea2AC (not a functional bug, but a latent confusion risk); renamed to match. Heavy normalizer performance: built HeavyNormalizerBenchmarkMain (descriptive, not JMH, since real native construction for these families only exists in nativeTest which is wired to the pinned Paper runtime jar) with pool-isolated timing (packets pre-built before the timed loop, so only the normalizer itself is measured); no pathological allocation found in item/container/chunk/entity-metadata normalization, all scaling linearly as expected; one real hot-path allocation problem found and fixed - entitySyncedData() rebuilt a 7-entry reflective lookup map on every call, memoizing it cut the 30-field case from 11679ns/19084 bytes per op to 4718ns/3357 bytes per op (60%/82% reduction) with no semantic change. Tests: 191 -> 210 (11 new PreLoginAdmissionAndAuditTest, 4 new BindingRaceTest, 4 new StaleControlAndResourceAccountingTest). No new inter-module dependency added, no approved Phase 0 Markdown modified.

heavyNormalizerBenchmark.methodology: Packets pre-built into a pool before timing starts; only PaperPacketNormalizer.normalize(...) itself is timed, isolating normalizer cost from native-object test-fixture construction. Allocation sampled via Runtime heap-used before/after a batch (imprecise under concurrent GC, sufficient to catch a gross regression).
